extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry / readers of Mochizuki's IUT series
extracted.subtask_description: Interpreting and applying the definitions, normalizations, and compatibility conditions for log-volumes, log-links, and related measure-theoretic constructions in the context of LGP-/lgp-Gaussian log-theta-lattices and associated prime-strips in IUT theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: LGP-/lgp-Gaussian log-theta-lattices
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish the LGP-Gaussian and lgp-Gaussian log-theta-lattices; either can be represented by the oriented-graph diagrams described, with vertical arrows as full log-links and horizontal arrows the lgp- or LGP-links between n,m Hodge theaters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper states the main interest will be the LGP-Gaussian log-theta-lattice (Remark 3.8.1). Either diagram may be symbolically represented by an oriented graph whose vertices correspond to the n,m Hodge theaters; this identification underlies later constructions (e.g., log-links mapping between theaters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Packet-normalization (nonarchimedean)
rubrics_metrics.description: Normalize pvQ-adic log-volumes so that multiplication of an element of M(−) by pv corresponds to adding the quantity −log(pv) ∈ R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in Proposition 3.9(i) for nonarchimedean direct summands; ensures consistent scaling behaviour of local log-volumes under multiplication by the uniformizer pv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Packet-normalization (archimedean)
rubrics_metrics.description: Normalize archimedean (radial) log-volumes so that multiplication of an element of M(−) by e corresponds to adding 1 = log(e) ∈ R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in Proposition 3.9(i) for complex archimedean direct summands; analogous to nonarchimedean packet-normalization but using e as base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procession-normalization (averaging)
rubrics_metrics.description: When working with collections of capsules in a procession, normalize log-volumes on products of M(−) by taking the average over the various capsules (the procession-normalization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 3.9(i) and Remark 3.9.3 specify that normalization for processions is obtained by averaging packet-normalized log-volumes across capsules; averaging (not arbitrary weighted averages) is required for compatibility with inclusion morphisms among capsules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invariance under permutations of labels A
rubrics_metrics.description: The local log-volume measures μlog_A,vQ (and related constructions) are invariant with respect to permutations of the index set A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated in Proposition 3.9(i) for both nonarchimedean and archimedean cases; ensures symmetry of log-volumes under relabeling of components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-analytic compatibility and functorial construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Log-volumes constructed on mono-analytic log-shells I†D_v (and I†F-variants) are compatible with the local holomorphic log-volumes via the natural poly-isomorphisms of Proposition 3.2(i); these log-volumes may be constructed functorially from the D-prime-strips under consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 3.9(ii) emphasizes that mono-analytic log-volumes arise by adjusting to account for discrepancies between holomorphic and mono-analytic integral structures, and are compatible (via poly-isomorphisms) with the packet-normalized holomorphic log-volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global log-volume by finite-sum of local log-volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: Define a global log-volume A,VQ : M(I_Q(AFVQ)) → R by adding the local log-volumes at vQ ∈ VQ (all but finitely many being zero) on components whose local log-volume is zero except for finitely many places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 3.9(iii) constructs the global log-volume by summation of local contributions, requires elements have zero local log-volume for all but finitely many vQ, and yields invariance under multiplication by (†M mod)_α and permutations of A; for certain J the global log-volume equals the degree of an arithmetic line bundle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-link compatibility of log-volumes across lattice indices
rubrics_metrics.description: Log-volumes associated to the objects appearing in constructions of local/global LGP-/lgp-monoids/Frobenioids are compatible relative to the log-link n,m−1HT → n,mHT: log-volumes indexed by (n,m) are compatible with those indexed by (n,m−1) at the level of Q-spans of log-shells, as in Propositions 1.2(iii) and 1.3(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 3.9(iv)(a,b) explicates that log-volumes determine consistent measures under the action of the log-link maps, which is essential for comparing volumes in the log-theta-lattice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of procession-normalization weights (must average equally)
rubrics_metrics.description: One cannot use more general weighted averages when defining procession-normalizations; equal averaging over capsules is necessary to ensure compatibility when components labeled j appear in multiple distinct capsules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.9.3 explains that because the same log-shell component may appear in different capsules, weights must be identical for those capsules to obtain a well-defined procession-normalization compatible with inclusion morphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of pre-ample and ample subsets / measure-space criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: A subset S ⊆ M is pre-ample if S is a relatively compact Borel set; pre-ample S is ample if μ_M(S) > 0; (M, μ_M) is ample if it admits an ample subset. Fn(M) consists of measurable f : M → R_≥0 with finite image and support in Sub(M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.9.4(i) introduces these measure-theoretic notions and uses them to build the algebraic/monoidal formalism (integration as R>0-equivariant surjection). These definitions control which subsets/functions are admissible in the reified semi-simplification formalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reified semi-simplification Rss(M) and integration quotient properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Integration over M gives an R>0-equivariant surjection Fn(M) → R_≥0; the quotient FnRssM : Fn(M) → Rss(M) identifies functions/sets with the same integrated measure and furnishes Rss(M) with a monoid structure and R>0-action compatible with unions and disjoint sums.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.9.4(i) spells out how Rss(M) is the quotient encoding 'measure data' as a monoid: it identifies subsets with equal measure, maps disjoint union to monoid sum, and behaves equivariantly under scaling by R>0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ample subset criterion for generating Rss(M)
rubrics_metrics.description: If E ⊆ Fn(M) is ample (i.e., R>0 · M(E) ≠ ∅), then the image Rss(E) ⊆ Rss(M) has R≥0-orbit equal to Rss(M); compact ample S gives Rss(S) ≅ Rss(M) up to R>0-action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in Remark 3.9.4(i) to reduce global Rss(M) considerations to compact ample subsets and to argue that a small ample region can generate the whole reified semi-simplification up to scaling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product compatibility: Rss(M1×M2) ≅ Rss(M1) ⊗ Rss(M2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For ample measure spaces (M1, μ1) and (M2, μ2), the product (M1×M2, μ1×μ2) is ample and there is a natural R>0-equivariant isomorphism Rss(M1) ⊗ Rss(M2) → Rss(M1×M2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.9.4(i) uses this to treat product spaces and to reason about tensor-product behavior of the monoids isomorphic to R_≥0; important when building Rss for direct-sum/tensor-product topological fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding ill-defined log-volumes modulo log(λ)
rubrics_metrics.description: If log-links dilate volumes by a factor λ ≠ 1, naive volume computations might only be well-defined modulo log(λ) in R / Z·log(λ), which is unacceptable for obtaining absolute log-volume estimates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.9.4(ii) explains this pathology via the Q_p example and motivates the need for the chosen normalization and Rss formalism to obtain well-defined real-valued log-volumes (not only modulo a lattice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Haar-normalization on local fields and equality μk(S) = μk(log_k(S))
rubrics_metrics.description: Equip local field k with Haar measure μ_k normalized so O_k has measure 1; for compact ample S ⊆ O_k^× on which log_k is injective, one has μ_k(S) = μ_k(log_k(S)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.9.4(iii) ties this normalization to compatibility of log-volume under the log map and to the reified semi-simplification diagram that identifies Rss(O_k^×) with Rss(k).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with finite extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of finite extensions k1 ⊆ k2 induces natural R>0-equivariant isomorphisms Rss(k1)^{⊗[k2:k1]} ≅ Rss(k2) compatible with the maps to R_≥0, reflecting behavior of Haar measures under finite extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.9.4(iii) shows how Haar-measure normalization and product decompositions yield compatibility of Rss and log-volume across finite extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-Kummer correspondence compatibility (bad/shifted valuations)
rubrics_metrics.description: When v ∈ V_bad with submonoid O_k^× × q^N ⊆ k, the log-Kummer operations (pass to O_k^× × q^N, then to O_k^×, then log_k, then to k) induce R>0-equivariant isomorphisms Rss(k) → Rss(O_k^×) → Rss(log_k(O_k^×)) → Rss(k) compatible with normalized log-volume, and the submonoid q^N embeds N → Rss(k) mapping 1 → −log(q).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.9.4(iv) describes how multiplicative submonoids interact with the Rss formalism and how the image of q^N is tracked in Rss(k) via the normalized log-volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topological tensor product normalization and tensor-power compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: For ki^A = ⊗_{α∈A} ki_α (topological tensor product), equip ki^A with Haar measure normalized so the ring of integers has measure 1; Rss(ki^A) carries log-link compatibility which is the d_α-th tensor power (or d_A-th tensor power) of compatibility for factors, functorially induced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.9.4(v) indicates one can reduce log-link compatibility for ki^A to that of its factors and to Q_p, independent of α, using the tensor-power descriptions and product-measure arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archimedean (complex) normalization and ρ_k identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Equip complex archimedean field k with standard Euclidean metric (O_k^× length 2π), obtain measures μ_|k| and μ_{O_k^×} making |k| and O_k^× ample, and construct an R>0-equivariant isomorphism ρ_k : Rss(O_k^×) ≅ Rss(|k|) and a commutative diagram linking O_k^×, |k|, log_k(O_k^×) and their Rss images compatible with log-volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.9.4(vi) provides the recipe for archimedean compatibility using exp/log and covering maps; normalization constants may be chosen to match the usual radial/angular log-volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holomorphic hull (hull) construction and characterization φ: P → H
rubrics_metrics.description: For relatively compact subset U in I_Q((−)), define its holomorphic hull as the smallest subset λ·O_{(−)} (with each component λ nonzero) containing U; if not relatively compact the hull is the whole space. The hull map φ: P → H satisfies (P1) φ(H)=H, (P2) P ⊆ φ(P), (P3) monotonicity φ(P1) ⊆ φ(P2) when P1 ⊆ P2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.9.5(i)-(ii) treats hulls as canonical 'holomorphic closures' of product regions and characterizes φ as a push-forward/splitting of the inclusion H ⊆ P; this map is central in later log-volume estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-volume hull-approximants Φ(P) and Ξ(P) and compact indeterminacy
rubrics_metrics.description: For P in P, define Φ(P) = {H ∈ H | φ(P) ⊇ H, μlog(H) ≥ μlog(P)} and Ξ(P) = {H ∈ H | φ(P) ⊇ H, μlog(H) = μlog(P)}. Elements of Φ(P) or Ξ(P) are 'log-volume approximations' of P by hulls, and all such approximants are contained in the compact set φ(P) (compactness of indeterminacy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.9.5(iii) emphasizes that indeterminacies are compact (contained in φ(P)), a deliberate design to keep all approximation choices controlled for log-volume estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for nonemptiness of Ξ(P)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ξ(P) is guaranteed nonempty under either: (Ξnon1) Galois-closure residue degrees dividing v_Q are 1 and μlog(P)=μlog(Q) for some Z_{p_vQ}-submodule Q ∈ P; or (Ξarc1) v_Q ∈ V_arc; globally the analogue of Ξ(P) is nonempty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.9.5(iv) lists sufficient conditions ensuring exact-log-volume hulls exist (Ξ(P) ≠ ∅). In general Ξ(P) may be empty; the global context including an archimedean place ensures nonemptiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat: hull enlargement can strictly increase log-volume
rubrics_metrics.description: Even when Ξ(P) ≠ ∅ or P ⊆ φ(P), it can happen that μlog(P) < μlog(H_Ξ(P)) ≤ μlog(φ(P)), so passing to hull-approximants may strictly increase log-volume (example in (Ξ3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remark 3.9.5(iv) warns that hulls used to approximate regions need not preserve log-volume, and one must account for possible strict inequalities when estimating log-volumes.
